syntheticNote: Synthetic stand-in built by ml/scripts/synthetic_fantasy.py, not a model forecast.

team.notes: Floor lowered from 4.5 to 3.0 for 2026 (fanamp, gridside). Transfers are counted as the net change versus the previous race in 2026 (fanamp). Free transfer count 2 is from earlier seasons and not restated in the 2026 text.

chips_and_multipliers.drs_boost: one driver per race scores x2 (always available)
chips_and_multipliers.notes: Chips (Limitless, Wildcard, Final Fix, Extra DRS x3, Autopilot, No Negative changed for 2026) affect a user's team score only, never the asset points or prices. Not needed for asset scoring.

price_change.applied: after every race weekend (gameday), before the next deadline
price_change.metric: points per million (PPM) = mean(asset fantasy points over its last N active gamedays) / current price, N = min(3, active gamedays so far)
price_change.points_used: the asset's official gameday total (qualifying + sprint + race), without chips or DRS boost
price_change.price_used: the asset price going into the gameday just scored (the current price, not the price at each race)
price_change.early_season: Rounds 1 and 2 average over 1 and 2 gamedays respectively. This is identical to the community description 'thresholds start lower (x1/3, x2/3) while missing races count as zero' with a fixed divisor of 3.
price_change.inactive_assets: An asset that is inactive for a gameday (driver replaced, reserve) keeps its price; its inactive gamedays are skipped in the rolling window.

bounds.notes: 2026: Mercedes went 33.8 -> 34.0 with a 'great' rating (+0.2 instead of +0.3), so 34.0 is a hard cap. 2025 had floor 4.5 and no cap (McLaren reached 36.1).

price_change.validation: reproduces 98.9% of 538 observed 2026 asset price changes (gamedays 1 to 16; 99.05% of active assets) and 99.1% of 689 observed 2025 changes; see data/raw/fantasy/validation.json
price_change.notes: Not published by the game. Remaining misses: two 2026 gameday 8 (Austria) changes consistent with post-race point corrections applied after the price update (Gasly, Lawson), and mid-season seat swaps (2025 Lawson/Tsunoda after round 2, 2026 Lawson/Tsunoda/Hadjar rounds 12 to 15) where the game moved prices between assets.
price_change.ppm_rounding: PPM rounded to 2 decimals before rating; 1.20 counts as great and 0.60 as terrible (fitted on 2025 boundary cases: 1.195 and 1.200 rated great, 0.601 rated terrible). Low confidence on the exact boundary handling.

driver.notes: NC applies to drivers who set no time in Q1, including inactive drivers in the game. A disqualified driver gets the -5 NC penalty and no position points; the extra DSQ penalty goes to the constructor.

constructor.progression_bonus_rule: only the single best applicable line is awarded

driver.notes: Sprint NC/DSQ reduced from -20 to -10 for 2026. Positions gained/lost use the official sprint starting grid vs the sprint classification; NC drivers get no gained/lost points. The game feeds label the sprint session 'Sprint Qualifying' although it is the sprint race.

Gained/lost: official FIA starting grid vs race classification, not the qualifying result. Pit lane starters count as starting behind the last car on the grid. Unclassified drivers get -20 and no gained/lost points. Overtakes keep counting for unclassified drivers. An overtake is valid when a driver legally passes another on track and the passed car was not entering or in the pit lane, not suffering a failure and not going unreasonably slow (official note); the counts come from F1's timing data and are not published elsewhere, so they can only be approximated (e.g. OpenF1 /overtakes).

constructor.world_record_holder: McLaren, Qatar 2023 (as stated in the 2026 rules text)
constructor.notes: Pit stop time is the stationary time (DHL timing), one band award per team from its fastest stop in the Grand Prix only (no sprint). In the playerstats feed the band award is labelled 'Fastest Pitstop' and the +5 overall fastest bonus is labelled '2nd Fastest Pitstop'. Band edges at exactly 2.00/2.20/2.50/3.00 s are assumed to fall into the slower band's upper bound as printed (e.g. 2.50-2.99 = 2 points).
